cvEn:
Meir Itzhak Harosh, son of Isha (Alice) and Avraham, was born in 1955 in Morocco.

A year after his birth, Meir's family immigrated to Israel and settled in Dimona, where he grew up and was educated.

In 1973 he enlisted in the IDF and served as a combatant in the Nahal Brigade. During his service he was promoted to Staff Sergeant.

On 4 December 1975, Meir was seriously injured in a traffic accident that occurred during an operational activity in the south of the country. He was hospitalized at Soroka Hospital, and a month later was transferred to Tel HaShomer Hospital, where he spent a year undergoing treatment and rehabilitation.

At the end of the rehabilitation period, Meir remained paralyzed in both legs. Nevertheless, he kept his optimism and did not let his disability stand in his way.

In 1979 Meir married Hanna. A deep love existed between them, and throughout their marriage Meir would give Hanna flowers as a sign of appreciation and love. Over the years they had five children, Ortal, Liran, Moran, Lior and Eliya, whom they raised with great love in their home in Dimona.

As his children grew up, Meir was blessed with fifteen grandchildren, and he enjoyed spending time in the embrace of his growing family.

Meir devoted his whole life to Torah, and faith was his way of life. The values that guided him were love of people, peace and unity. He never spoke ill of others and kept away from any speech that could harm another. He was a man of kindness and giving, who acted discreetly, quietly and modestly, without asking anything for himself. For example, he would buy tefillin for people who could not afford them, and he donated part of his disability allowance to those in need. He was also deeply interested in current affairs and sports, and was a fan of the "Maccabi Tel Aviv" basketball team.

Meir Itzhak Harosh passed away on the 14th of Adar 5786 (3 March 2026), at the age of seventy. He was laid to rest in the cemetery in Dimona. He is survived by his wife, five children and siblings.

On his headstone his loved ones wrote: "He walks in innocence, does justice, and speaks truth in his heart."
